extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and instructors in commutative algebra (students reading solutions to exercises)
extracted.subtask_description: Solution notes and worked exercises in commutative algebra covering flatness, integral dependence, localization, support, and related structural results; intended to guide learning and checking proofs for standard textbook exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor identity for quotient modules
rubrics_metrics.description: R/a ⊗_R R/b = R/(a + b) (and R/a ⊗ R/b = R/(a+b) = R/(a+b) by cited identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute tensor products of quotient modules; e.g., to reduce R/a ⊗ R/b to a single quotient and apply further properties (see usage in proofs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of nonzero vector spaces over a field is nonzero (8.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is a field and M and N are nonzero k-vector spaces, then M ⊗_k N ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: write M,N as free vector spaces and use M ⊗_k N ≅ k^(dim M * dim N); in particular k ⊗_k k = k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear functors preserve finite direct sums (8.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any linear functor F : (R-mod) → (R-mod) preserves finite direct sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moreover, the canonical map M ⊗ F(R) → F(M) is surjective if F preserves surjections and M is finitely generated, and is an isomorphism if F preserves cokernels and M is finitely presented. Use characterization of finite direct sums in terms of maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change of flat modules (9.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R' is a flat R-algebra and P is a flat R'-module, then P is flat as an R-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cancellation: (– ⊗_R R') ⊗_{R'} P = – ⊗_R P; exactness of intermediate tensors implies exactness of the composition, hence flatness over R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensoring a flat module with an algebra yields flat module over the algebra (9.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a flat R-module and R' an R-algebra, then M ⊗_R R' is a flat R'-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cancellation and exactness: (M ⊗_R R') ⊗_{R'} – ≅ M ⊗_R – to show exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: If R/a is flat then a = a^2 (9.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a be an ideal. If R/a is flat as an R-module then a is idempotent: a = a^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses tensoring the inclusion a → R with R/a: injection plus vanishing image forces a = a^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for faithful flatness (9.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R' an R-algebra, the following are equivalent: (1) R' is faithfully flat; (2) every ideal a of R equals the contraction of its extension a = φ^{-1}(aR'); (3) every prime p of R is the contraction of some prime q of R'; (4) every maximal m of R extends to a proper ideal mR' ≠ R'; (5) every nonzero R-module M remains nonzero after tensoring: M ⊗_R R' ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The solution proves (1)⇒(2)⇒(3)⇒(4)⇒(5)⇒(1) using elementary properties: injectivity of R/a→R'/aR', prime contraction, and passage to nonzero modules via localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local flat homomorphism is faithfully flat (9.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ:A→B is a local homomorphism of local rings (φ(m_A) ⊆ m_B) and φ is flat, then φ is faithfully flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from the equivalent conditions for faithful flatness because maximal ideals extend to proper ideals under the local map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change for Hom and finite generation/presentation (9.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a canonical map Hom_R(M,N) ⊗_R R' → Hom_{R'}(M ⊗_R R', N ⊗_R R'). If R' is flat over R and M is finitely generated then the map is injective; if M is finitely presented then it is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct by functoriality and use finite generation/presentation hypotheses with flatness to pass kernels/cokernels through tensoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equational criterion for flatness (9.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformulation: M is flat iff for every relation Σ_i x_i y_i = 0 (x_i∈R, y_i∈M) there exist x_{ij}∈R and y'_j∈M with y_i = Σ_j x_{ij} y'_j for all i and Σ_i x_i x_{ij} = 0 for all j (equation (9.19.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the matrix/factorization viewpoint: relations lift through a map R^m → M factoring through R^n if and only if one can express the y_i via a combination whose coefficients satisfy those linear relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat modules over domains are torsion-free; converse over PID (9.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a domain and M is flat, then M is torsion-free. Conversely, if R is a PID and M is torsion-free then M is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward direction: multiplication by nonzero x on R is injective, so after tensoring it's injective on M. Converse uses ideal generated by x and the ideal criterion for flatness for PIDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique idempotent generator for finitely generated idempotent ideal (10.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a is a finitely generated idempotent ideal (a = a^2) then there is a unique idempotent e with ⟨e⟩ = a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction via previous results (10.3) producing e∈a with (1−e)a = 0, hence a = ⟨e⟩ and e^2 = e; uniqueness follows from idempotent uniqueness lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for absolutely flat rings (10.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are equivalent: (1) R is absolutely flat (every module is flat); (2) every finitely generated ideal is a direct summand of R; (3) every finitely generated ideal is idempotent; (4) every principal ideal is idempotent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chain of implications shown: (1)⇒(2) using R/a flat ⇒ splitting, (2)⇔(3) via prior result, (4) trivial⇒(3), and (4)⇒(3) via decomposing generators into idempotents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of absolute flatness (10.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Boolean, then R is absolutely flat. Quotients of absolutely flat rings are absolutely flat. In an absolutely flat ring every nonunit is a zero-divisor; if additionally local then R is a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use idempotence of all elements in Boolean rings, passing idempotence to quotients, and algebraic manipulations to show nonunits force zero divisors, and in the local case only 0 is nonunit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakayama-type surjection plus smallness implies isomorphism (10.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M→N and another map with image in mN for m in rad(R). If the first map is surjective and the second has image in mN, then sum map is an isomorphism on finitely generated modules under hypotheses (uses Nakayama).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: reduction mod m, use surjectivity and finiteness to deduce that the map on localization is surjective; apply previously proved lemmas to deduce bijectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal generating sets via residue field (10.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A local, M finitely generated, elements m1,...,mn map to m'_i in M/mM. Then m'_1,...,m'_n form a basis for M/mM iff m1,...,mn form a minimal generating set of M. All minimal generating sets have same cardinality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is reduction modulo maximal ideal plus Nakayama's lemma: minimal generators correspond bijectively to bases of M/mM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakayama corollaries: vanishing and tensor nonvanishing (10.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) For A local, M=0 iff M ⊗_A k = 0. (2) If M≠0 and N≠0 finitely generated modules then M ⊗_A N ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Nakayama: M = 0 iff M/mM = 0. For tensor nonvanishing reduce to residue field and use earlier result that tensor of nonzero vector spaces is nonzero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements integral over invariants under finite group action (10.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If finite group G acts on a domain R with ring of invariants R', then every x∈R is integral over R' (indeed over the subring generated by elementary symmetric functions of G-conjugates of x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct monic polynomial F(X) = ∏_{g∈G} (X − g(x)); coefficients are invariant, so F(x)=0 gives integral dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cayley–Hamilton integral dependence example (10.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given k field, P=k[X] and R=k[X^2], any f∈P satisfies a degree-2 monic equation over R (explicit via matrix of multiplication and characteristic polynomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split f into even and odd parts fe+fo with fo=gX; form 2×2 matrix and apply Cayley–Hamilton to get quadratic relation over R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product of integrally closed algebras is integral (10.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R1,...,Rn are R-algebras integral over R then their product ∏_i R_i is integral over R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: show each element has components integral, and the subalgebra generated by the components is module-finite over R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality testing componentwise for product rings (10.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R = ∏_i R_i ⊆ R' = ∏_i R'_i and x=(x_i) in R', x is integral over R iff each x_i is integral over R_i; likewise R integrally closed in R' iff each R_i integrally closed in R'_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct coordinate-wise monic polynomials and combine them into a polynomial over R; conversely project equations coordinatewise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saturation/localization criteria (11.2, 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: S^{-1}R = 0 iff S contains a nilpotent element. For saturation T and map φ, describe T as {x/s | x∈S, s∈S} and show φ_S(T)=S (properties of saturations and universal maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use construction of localization to see when 1/1=0 and apply multiplicativity to pass between sets and their images under localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate subrings of Q are localizations of Z (11.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every intermediate ring Z ⊆ R ⊆ Q is S^{-1}Z where S is multiplicative set generated by primes appearing in denominators of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given R, collect primes appearing in denominators in lowest terms; elements of R are then exactly fractions with denominators in S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization behavior of ideals (11.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a⊆b then aS ⊆ bS; (aS)S = aS; and (aS bS)S = (ab)S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use generators and multiplicativity to establish the inclusions and equalities by double inclusion arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilradical commutes with localization (11.16)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by writing elements as x/s and passing powers through denominators, using saturation to move back and forth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves integrality (11.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R' is integral over R then S^{-1}R' is integral over S^{-1}R for any multiplicative S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take an integral equation for x∈R' and divide coefficients by suitable powers of s to produce an integral equation after localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral closure yields fraction-field description (11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is integrally closed in finite field extension L of K = Frac(R), then every element x∈L can be written x = b/a with b∈R and a∈R; L is the fraction field of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear denominators in the minimal polynomial to produce b and a with b=ax ∈ R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of localization making algebra module-finite (11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R' is finitely generated R-algebra and Frac(R') is finite-dimensional over Frac(R), then there exists f∈R such that R'_f is module-finite over R_f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express generators as integral elements after multiplying by denominators to obtain elements integral over R_f; use finiteness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutation and description of iterated localizations (11.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various equalities: (1) with T' the image of T in S^{-1}R, T^{-1}R = T'^{-1}(S^{-1}R) = T^{-1}(S^{-1}R) when S⊆T; (2) if U={st | s∈S,t∈T} then T^{-1}(S^{-1}R)=S^{-1}(T^{-1}R)=U^{-1}R; (3) if S'={t' | t' t ∈ S for some t} then S'^{-1}R = S^{-1}R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use universal properties of localization and multiplicative closure to equate iterated localization constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization and normalization commute (11.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: For domain R and multiplicative S not containing 0, normalization/localization commute: normalization of S^{-1}R equals S^{-1} of normalization of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integrality and clearing denominators to pass integral equations back and forth between R and S^{-1}R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of S^{-1}M being M (12.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For module M, M = S^{-1}M if and only if M is naturally an S^{-1}R-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If M already admits S^{-1}R-action, it satisfies the universal property of localization; conversely localization yields the module structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated localization of modules (12.5)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show both constructions satisfy the same universal property and factorization properties with respect to maps into T^{-1}R-modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered colimit description of localization (12.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: S becomes a filtered category with Hom(s,t) = {x∈R | x s = t}; S^{-1}M is the colimit of the functor s↦M (with transition maps given by multiplication), i.e., lim_{→} M_s ≅ S^{-1}M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct maps m/s as images of elements in the directed system and show the universal property and injectivity/surjectivity to get isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization annihilation criterion for modules (12.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: S^{-1}M = 0 if Ann(M) ∩ S ≠ ∅. Conversely, if M is finitely generated and S^{-1}M = 0 then Ann(M) ∩ S ≠ ∅.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward: an annihilator in S kills all localized elements. Reverse for finitely generated M: choose generators and find denominators annihilating each generator, multiply to get element of S annihilating M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves projectivity (12.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is projective over R then S^{-1}P is projective over S^{-1}R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express P as a direct summand of a free module and localize: locality preserves direct summands and freeness, hence projectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization commutes with tensor product (12.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: S^{-1}(M ⊗_R N) = S^{-1}M ⊗_R N = S^{-1}M ⊗_{S^{-1}R} S^{-1}N = S^{-1}M ⊗_R S^{-1}N, with canonical identifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use associativity and cancellation of tensor product with localization and check kernel generators vanish after appropriate isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterexample: map on Homs not injective after localization (12.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist modules M (infinite direct sums of Z/n) for which the canonical map R → Hom_R(M,M) is injective but after localization S^{-1} the induced map need not be injective (map of (12.21) may fail injectivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct M with torsion so that S^{-1}M = 0 but Hom(S^{-1}M,S^{-1}M)=0, showing failure of injection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed points in Spec(R) are maximal ideals (13.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prime p is a closed point (i.e., {p} is closed) in Spec(R) iff p is maximal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p maximal then V(p)={p}. Conversely, if p not maximal it's contained in some maximal m so closure of {p} contains m and is not equal to {p}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful flatness corresponds to surjectivity on Spec (13.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-algebra R' is faithfully flat over R iff the induced map Spec(R') → Spec(R) is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the geometric restatement of equivalent conditions for faithful flatness (see 9.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-compact open subsets characterized by finitely generated ideals (13.5)
rubrics_metrics.description:
An open U ⊆ Spec(R) is quasi-compact iff its complement X
t = V(a) for a finitely generated ideal a; equivalently U = ∪_{i=1}^n D(f_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard opens D(f) and finiteness of generators to cover and invoke quasi-compactness of D(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spec of a Boolean ring is compact Hausdorff; clopen sets are D(f) (13.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is Boolean then Spec(B) is compact Hausdorff; subsets that are both open and closed are precisely the D(f) for f∈B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses idempotence of elements, relationship between D(f) and D(1−f), and Chinese remainder style arguments to get Hausdorff and compactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and specialization (13.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p ∈ Supp(M) then V(p) ⊆ Supp(M) (i.e., every specialization of p lies in the support of M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For q⊇p, localization satisfies M_p ≠ 0 ⇒ M_q ≠ 0 by localization properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of Q/Z (13.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For M = Q/Z considered as a Z-module, Supp(M) is the set of all nonzero primes of Z; Supp(M) is not Zariski-closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute localizations: at p≠0, Z_p ≠ Q_p so Q_p/Z_p ≠ 0; at 0 the module vanishes, showing support excludes 0 and cannot be V(a) for any ideal a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of submodules detected at maximal localizations (13.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M and N are submodules of P and M_m = N_m for every maximal ideal m, then M = N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider quotient N/M; if it vanishes at every maximal ideal it vanishes globally by previously proved lemmas (using localization and finiteness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducedness detected locally (13.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: R is reduced iff S^{-1}R is reduced for all multiplicative S iff R_m is reduced for all maximal ideals m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use behavior of nilradical under localization and detection of nilpotents via localizations at maximals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal primes and product decomposition (13.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If R_p is a domain for every prime p then minimal primes are pairwise comaximal. (2) If R_p is a domain for every p and the set of minimal primes is finite, then R ≅ ∏_{i=1}^n R/p_i with each factor a domain, and conversely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Chinese Remainder and injectivity of canonical map to product of residue rings, plus localization arguments to see domain properties coordinatewise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating sets detected modulo maximal ideals (13.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements m_i generate module M iff for every maximal m their images generate M_m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the map from free module to M and check surjectivity on each localization; apply standard lemma that surjectivity is detected locally for finitely generated modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization at primes of integral extensions is faithfully flat (13.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R→R' is integral and p' a prime over p then R'_{p'} is faithfully flat over R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine integrality, localization properties, and the fact that a flat local homomorphism with image of maximal ideal contained in maximal is faithfully flat (use 9.10 & 9.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free of rank n characterization (13.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module P is locally free of rank n iff P is finitely generated and for every maximal ideal m, P_m ≅ R_m^n. Moreover, for any p∈Spec(R) there exists f∉p with P_f ≅ R_f^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use finite generation to produce surjection from R^n and then local criteria plus Nakayama to lift to isomorphism on some neighborhood D(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semilocal locally free modules are free (13.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is semilocal and P is locally free of rank n, then P is free of rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that over semilocal rings finitely presented projective modules with constant local rank are globally free.
